To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
IGF-I triggers stimulatory actions in mesotheliomas and lung tumors through both IGF-1R and GPER as well as IGF-1 R and DDR1.
IGF-I promotes chemotaxis and cell migration of mesothelioma cells through a functional cross-talk between IGF-IR, GPER and DDR-1.
IGF-I stimulates the expression of GPER and DDR-1 and their main target genes, thus leading to increased cell migration.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a novel mechanism by which IGF-I triggers stimulatory actions in aggressive tumors as lung and mesothelioma.
the molecular mechanisms through IGF-I/ IGF-IR system promotes the cross-talk with GPR30 and DDR1 in cancer cells.
the identification of novel therapeutic strategies for the treatment of mesothelioma.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

IGF-I triggers the activation of a signaling cascade mediated by IGF-I-R, GPER, and DDR1 in cancer cells, leading to a functional crosstalk between these receptors and to an up-regulation of the expression of their target genes, thus resulting in the promotion of cancer cell chemotaxis, migration, and invasion.
IGF-I promotes the activation of the transduction network of IGF-IR, GPER, and DDR1, and the consequent expression of target genes in both mesothelial and lung cancer cells.
IGF-I promotes mesothelioma cell proliferation and migration through the activation of IGF-IR/GPER/DDR1 signaling network.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
IGF-I triggers stimulatory actions in mesotheliomas and lung tumors through a novel functional cross-talk between GPER and DDR.

IGF-I promotes cell migration through the cooperation of IGF-IR, GPER and DDR-1.
The main takeaway from our work is that
IGF-I stimulates the expression of both GPER and its target genes CTGF, EGR1 and DDR1 as well as DDR1 target genes such as MATN-2 and FBN-1.
IGF-I promotes cell migration and invasion in both mesothelial and lung cancer cell lines.
IGF-I triggers a functional cross-communication between IGF-IR, GPER and DDR-1 in aggressive mesothelioma tumors and lung tumors.
